planting.note: Plant rhizome divisions or container stock in spring in moist, humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial shade to full sun, giving the wiry, climbing stems a fence, shrub, or trellis to scramble over.

directions: Smilax china is the East Asian vine for which North America's false chinaroot (Smilax pseudochina) is named in reference, sharing the same tendril-climbing habit but armed with noticeably sharper, more numerous prickles along its wiry stems. Small greenish spring flowers give way to round berries that ripen bright red rather than the blue-black fruit typical of American greenbriers, persisting on the vine into winter. Like its North American namesake, it stores energy in a thickened underground rhizome that has long been dug, dried, and processed into a starchy food and traditional remedy across its native China, Japan, and Korea. Grow it at a woodland edge or along a fence in moist, humus-rich soil in partial shade to full sun, and expect it to keep its thorny armor even in a small garden bed where false chinaroot would stay unarmed.
